Chapter One: Recognizing and Questioning Inherited Life Rules.
Have you ever noticed how, without even thinking about it, you follow a set of invisible instructions in your daily life? These unwritten rules come from all sorts of places—family, culture, school, even the media. And, whether you realize it or not, they shape everything—from the way you see success, to what you think happiness looks like.
In this book, there’s a name for these inherited beliefs: “Brules.” That’s short for “bullshit rules.” Now, these Brules aren’t always meant to harm you. But here’s the thing—they’re often outdated, they can hold you back, and honestly, they were never really created with your unique fulfillment in mind.
Just picture someone who’s convinced that being successful means working long hours at a traditional job—even if it brings them zero joy. Maybe this belief was handed down by their parents, or it’s just what everyone around them seems to do. Over time, these old rules settle in, quietly running the show and narrowing what feels possible.
So, what if you could hit pause for a moment and really look at these scripts you’re living by? Think of it like updating your phone: before you can add cool new features, you’ve got to clear out the old, buggy software. Your mind works the same way. When you start questioning which beliefs actually help you thrive—and which ones are just leftovers from someone else’s era—you open the door to a whole new way of living.
Here’s a simple way to start:
First, notice your automatic thoughts—especially those that make you feel stuck or uneasy. Next, ask yourself: where did this belief come from? Was it your family, your school, something you saw on TV, or just the culture around you? Finally, check in—does this rule really line up with who you want to be, and what you value most?
Take the classic idea that “you have to own a home to be successful.” Maybe your parents always said that—because for them, it made sense in their time. But your reality might be totally different. By questioning that old belief, you can start defining success on your own terms, in a way that actually fits your life.
This is where the real journey starts. Before you can build something amazing, you’ve got to clear out the mental clutter of all those unexamined rules. Questioning isn’t about rebelling just for the sake of it. It’s about making space to choose what matters to you—on purpose. It’s your chance to become the architect of your own reality, instead of just following a script that was written for someone else.
